subtitle: Explore pitch shifting, octave effects, and harmonizers for creating unique harmonic textures

introduction.title: Understanding Pitch Effects
introduction.text: Pitch effects manipulate the fundamental frequency of your guitar signal, creating everything from subtle detuning to dramatic octave shifts. These effects can double your guitar parts with harmony lines, create bass-like low octaves, or transport your sound into entirely new frequency ranges. From the classic octave fuzz of Hendrix to the complex harmonies of modern metal, pitch effects open up new sonic territories.
introduction.quote: Pitch effects don't just change what you play—they multiply it, creating ensembles from single notes and transforming your guitar into an orchestra of harmonic possibilities.

cards.title: Detection Methods
cards.description: Pitch effects first detect the fundamental frequency of your guitar signal, then generate new frequencies based on mathematical relationships to create harmony, octaves, or entirely different pitches.
items: Analog Frequency Doubling: Simple, fast, vintage character
Digital Pitch Tracking: Accurate, complex harmonies possible
Polyphonic Detection: Tracks multiple notes simultaneously
Monophonic Detection: Single note at a time, more reliable

cards.title: Challenges
items: Tracking speed and accuracy
Handling complex chords
Maintaining natural sound quality
Avoiding glitches and artifacts

cards.title: Octave Effects
cards.description: Generate a signal exactly one octave (12 semitones) above or below your original note. Octave up doubles the frequency, octave down halves it.

fields.label: Common Types
fields.value: Octave Up: Adds brightness and presence. Octave Down: Creates bass-like low end. Dual Octave: Both up and down simultaneously.

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Lead guitar: Adding sparkle and cutting power. Bass simulation: Creating low-end thickness. Organ-like textures: Multiple octaves together. 12-string guitar simulation.

fields.label: Famous Example
fields.value: Jimi Hendrix's "Purple Haze" intro uses octave fuzz.

cards.title: Pitch Shifters
cards.description: Shift pitch by any interval—not just octaves. Can create harmonies in specific keys, detune effects, or dramatic pitch bends.

fields.label: Key Features
fields.value: Variable pitch intervals, real-time pitch bending, multiple voices simultaneously, mix control for blend with dry signal

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Harmonized guitar solos, detuning for alternative tunings, creating interval harmonies (3rds, 5ths, etc.), special effects and sound design

fields.label: Pro Tip
fields.value: Use expression pedal control for smooth pitch bends and dives.

cards.title: Intelligent Harmonizers
cards.description: Analyze your playing and automatically generate harmonies based on selected keys and scales. More musically intelligent than simple pitch shifters.

fields.label: Advanced Features
fields.value: Key and scale selection, multiple harmony voices, voice leading and chord progressions, real-time key changes

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Professional studio harmonies, live performance enhancement, complex arrangement creation, jazz and fusion harmony

fields.label: Example Units
fields.value: TC Electronic VoiceLive, Eventide H9 Harmonizer

cards.title: Whammy/Dive Bomb Effects
cards.description: Real-time pitch shifting controlled by an expression pedal, simulating the effect of a whammy bar or creating dramatic pitch dives and climbs.

fields.label: Control Options
fields.value: Expression pedal for real-time control, preset intervals (octave, fifth, etc.), momentary footswitch triggering, customizable pitch ranges

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Rock and metal lead effects, simulating extreme whammy bar use, creating impossible pitch intervals, sound effects and noise music

fields.label: Famous User
fields.value: Tom Morello (Rage Against the Machine) signature technique

cards.title: Common Intervals
items: Perfect 5th (+7 semitones): Strong, stable harmony
Major 3rd (+4 semitones): Sweet, consonant harmony
Minor 3rd (+3 semitones): Darker, more complex
Perfect 4th (+5 semitones): Open, suspended sound
Octave (+12 semitones): Same note, different register

cards.title: Key-Based Harmonies
items: Diatonic Harmonies: Stay within the key signature
Parallel Intervals: Same interval throughout
Voice Leading: Smooth movement between chords
Modal Harmonies: Based on different modes
Example: In C major, harmonizing with 3rds: C→E, D→F, E→G, F→A, etc.

cards.title: "Purple Haze" - Jimi Hendrix
cards.description: Octavia octave-up fuzz on the intro riff

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Octave-up frequency doubling, combined with fuzz distortion, full wet signal (no dry blend), analog frequency multiplication

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates otherworldly psychedelic texture, adds cutting treble presence, defines the song's alien character, influenced generations of rock guitarists

cards.title: "My Sharona" - The Knack
cards.description: Octave-down effect on the bass line

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Octave-down pitch shifting, blended with original guitar, clean signal path, simulates bass guitar

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates thick low-end foundation, adds harmonic richness, fills out the arrangement, demonstrates octave-down utility

cards.title: "Bulls on Parade" - Rage Against the Machine
cards.description: DigiTech Whammy for radical pitch bends

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Expression pedal controlled, wide pitch range (2+ octaves), aggressive digital character, used for rhythmic emphasis

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates aggressive modern sound, adds rhythmic and melodic interest, defines Tom Morello's signature style, influences alternative and nu-metal

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Intelligent harmonizer, perfect 5th and 3rd intervals, key-based harmony generation, mixed with original signal

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates full orchestral guitar sound, adds sophistication to solos, supports progressive rock complexity, demonstrates musical harmony usage

fields.label: Clean Signal Input
fields.value: Pitch detection works best with clean, undistorted signals. Place pitch effects early in your chain.

fields.label: Single Note Playing
fields.value: Monophonic pitch effects track single notes more reliably than chords or complex intervals.

fields.label: Attack Sensitivity
fields.value: Consistent pick attack helps tracking accuracy. Compression before pitch effects can help.

fields.label: Signal Chain Position
fields.value: Guitar → Compression → Pitch Effects → Distortion → Modulation → Time Effects

fields.label: Playing Technique
fields.value: Clean, articulate playing improves tracking. Avoid overlapping notes when possible.

fields.label: Latency Awareness
fields.value: Digital pitch effects introduce small delays. Account for this in timing-critical situations.

cards.title: Layering Techniques
cards.description: Combine multiple pitch effects for complex textures

fields.label: Octave Stacking
fields.value: Original + Octave up + Octave down creates organ-like textures with massive, full-frequency sound. Great for power chords and riffs.

fields.label: Interval Combinations
fields.value: Mix multiple harmony intervals. Create chord-like textures from single notes. Build complex harmonic structures. Experiment with dissonant intervals.

cards.title: Expression Control
cards.description: Real-time pitch manipulation for dynamic performances

fields.label: Real-Time Pitch Bending
fields.value: Expression pedal for smooth transitions, create impossible pitch ranges, simulate extreme whammy bar effects, add movement to sustained notes

fields.label: Momentary Effects
fields.value: Quick octave jumps for emphasis, temporary harmonies on key notes, rhythmic pitch accents, dynamic arrangement enhancement

cards.title: Feedback and Self-Oscillation
cards.description: Some pitch effects can create feedback loops and self-generating tones
items: Set up regenerative feedback circuits
Create evolving harmonic drones
Use for ambient and experimental music
Control with expression for dynamic textures

cards.title: What to Avoid
items: Using pitch effects on overly distorted signals
Playing complex chords through monophonic pitch shifters
Ignoring the musical context and key
Over-relying on effects instead of developing technique
Not considering mix implications of frequency doubling
Using harmonies that clash with other instruments

cards.title: Best Practices
items: Start with clean signals for best tracking
Understand basic music theory for harmony
Use pitch effects to enhance, not replace, musical ideas
Practice clean playing technique first
Consider how effects fit in the full mix
Learn when NOT to use pitch effects

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Interval Recognition
items: Practice single notes with different pitch shift intervals
Play C note, add perfect 5th (G) harmony
Try major 3rd (E), minor 3rd (E♭), perfect 4th (F)
Notice how each interval creates different emotional colors
Practice with different root notes to hear interval consistency

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Octave Layering
items: Experiment with octave combinations on power chords
Play a simple power chord (E5, A5, D5)
Add octave up for brightness
Add octave down for bass foundation
Try all three together for massive sound

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Melody Harmonization
items: Take a simple melody and practice adding harmonies
Start with Mary Had a Little Lamb or similar simple melody
Set harmonizer to key of G major
Try different harmony intervals (3rd, 5th, 6th)
Notice how some intervals work better than others
